{"id":"project:kmp:decision:storage-seam","kind":"decision","text":"Step 1 of ADR-018 (PR #18, merged): a table-level storage seam in kmp-adapter-embedded — eleven key-to-bytes maps, four key shapes (Str, Str2, Str3, U64), exactly eight operations (get, insert, remove, ordered scan, scan by first key component, last of a u64 table, count, clear). Port logic (graph BFS, revision checks, idempotency) is written once against it; no port file names an engine type. Dispatch is dynamic (Arc<dyn Engine>) so EmbeddedKernelStore stays one concrete type and a single binary can carry two engines and pick at open time without generics climbing into kmp-embedded/kmp-mcp. redb keeps its exact on-disk layout (same typed TableDefinitions, unit-valued tables stay `()` because redb records value type names). Tables are opened per operation because a redb write txn refuses a second live handle and holding handles across seam calls would need a self-referential struct. Two contracts the ports relied on implicitly are now written: rows come back in ascending key order (byte-wise per component), and a never-written table reads as empty. Known cost: full projection rebuild +43% (2.3s→3.3s over 100k events) from per-op table open; fix would be a batch op on the seam, deferred until it matters.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"agentic_process","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:adr-018-multi-process","observed_at":"unix:101786886400:000000000","sequence":1}],"metadata":{"writer_actor":"claude-code","writer_intent":"record_decision"}}

{"id":"project:kmp:constraint:format-version-names-layout","kind":"constraint","text":"FORMAT_VERSION in a data directory names the LAYOUT (which engine wrote store/, and how), not the logical event format: 1 = redb (store/kernel.redb), 2 = SQLite (store/kernel.sqlite3). A SQLite store MUST stamp 2 because the version number is the only gate a binary that predates ADR-018 honours: a 0.1.x binary opening a SQLite directory would read 1, look for kernel.redb, not find it, and create an empty one beside the real store — silent empty memory, the exact failure ADR-012 forbids. With 2 it stops with 'newer than this binary supports; upgrade the binary'. The logical event format lives in its own constant EVENT_FORMAT_VERSION (=1 on both engines; it is what bundles carry). A store is never reopened as another engine's: the mismatch is refused by name in both directions. A binary built without the sqlite feature recognises 2 and names the feature to enable, stamping nothing.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"agentic_process","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:adr-018-multi-process","observed_at":"unix:101786888800:000000000","sequence":1}],"metadata":{"writer_actor":"claude-code","writer_intent":"record_decision"}}

{"id":"project:kmp:success:sqlite-engine-verified","kind":"success_path","text":"Step 2 of ADR-018 (PR #19, merged): the SQLite engine behind the seam passed its acceptance criteria. {"id":"project:kmp:decision:migration-is-replay","kind":"decision","text":"PR #20 (merged): a store changes engines by replaying its event log into a fresh directory of the other engine — the same operation a format bump has always been, because the append-only event log is the source of truth and projections are derived (ADR-009 Consequences promised this in July: 'revisiting this decision is an adapter swap, not a redesign'). User command: `kmp-mcp migrate <old-dir> <new-dir> --engine sqlite`. The receipt records both layouts (source_format 1, destination_format 2) plus the source sha256; the source is left byte-for-byte as it was. Proof of correctness is a single assertion: bundles exported from source and destination are byte-identical, because a bundle IS the event log and knows no engine. Direction SQLite→redb is REFUSED with the reason: WAL keeps committed data in the -wal sidecar until checkpointed, so 'copy the store file and read the copy' (what the redb migration does) would silently drop the newest events; a consistent snapshot (VACUUM INTO) is separate, undone work. Also: FORMAT_VERSION values below 1 are treated as redb sources (older layouts were all redb) so the a_store_this_binary_refuses_to_open_can_still_be_migrated path keeps working.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"agentic_process","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:adr-018-multi-process","observed_at":"unix:101786894200:000000000","sequence":1}],"metadata":{"writer_actor":"claude-code","writer_intent":"record_decision"}}

{"id":"project:kmp:decision:engine-selection-refuses-mismatch","kind":"decision","text":"Step 3 of ADR-018 (PR #21, merged): KMP_MCP_ENGINE=redb|sqlite decides only what a FRESH data directory becomes. An existing directory always opens with the engine it was created with, and asking for a different one is REFUSED by name (message carries `kmp-mcp migrate <this-dir> <new-dir> --engine <wanted>`), not warned-and-ignored — opening the wrong engine behind a user's back is the silent divergence that ends in 'why can't my second host open it'. Startup line names the engine ('kernel in-process, sqlite engine'); `kmp-mcp --version` lists layouts the build opens ('store formats 1, 2 (sqlite)'); the generic 'set KMP_KERNEL_GRPC_ENDPOINT...' hint no longer follows a store that refused to open. The doctor reads the engine off FORMAT_VERSION: on sqlite a second holder is reported green ('sqlite shares it'), on redb the single-writer warning ends with the migrate command with the real data dir filled in. The kernel's ADR-011 lock hint now keys on redb's own text 'Cannot acquire lock' rather than any 'could not open'. Docs: docs/operations/mcp-stdio.md 'Sharing one memory between two agent hosts' (install with --features sqlite; KMP_MCP_ENGINE for fresh, migrate for existing; point both hosts at it; costs stated; crates.io binary and plugin bundles are default builds without the engine).","coordinates":[{"dimension":"agentic_process","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:adr-018-multi-process","observed_at":"unix:101786898400:000000000","sequence":1}],"metadata":{"writer_actor":"claude-code","writer_intent":"record_decision"}}

{"id":"project:kmp:obs:catchup-needed-no-new-move","kind":"observation","text":"Use case 1 of the chosen three (PR #24) needed NO new capability: 'what happened since I last looked' was already two existing moves. kernel_rewind from now with limit 1 and budget.detail='full' returns the newest entry with coordinates[].observed_at (the bookmark) and page.total; kernel_forward from that timestamp returns exactly the entries after it with page.has_more. The non-obvious part is detail='full' — without it coordinates come back with occurred_at null and the bookmark is unobtainable, which is why nobody would have guessed the pattern. So the PR adds no eleventh move (the ten are a design constraint, not just a tagline) and instead adds reach: /kmp:catchup, /kmp-catchup for Codex, and a 'Catching up' section in the skill. Design rule recorded in the skill: the kernel deliberately does not remember where each reader got to — a memory that tracked its readers would keep state about the reader rather than about the work, and would need a reader identity the protocol does not have. {"id":"project:kmp:decision:memory-in-the-repo","kind":"decision","text":"Use case 2 of 3 (PR #26): `kmp-mcp export`/`import` with no path mean the project's committed memory at `.kmp/memory.jsonl`, the root the data-dir rule already walks up to find. Constant, not a setting, so the commands mean the same in every checkout and a reviewer knows where to look. `.kernel/` stays machine state and gitignored; the bundle belongs to the repo like a migration. Design calls: only a project-scoped store gets the default — an explicit KMP_MCP_DATA_DIR or the per-user store belongs to no repository and both commands refuse naming the resolution rule that won rather than guessing a file; export creates `.kmp/` on first save because failing there would make the convention useless exactly once per repo, at the moment someone first tries it; /kmp:restore is written to refuse rather than help, since import requires an empty store (restore, not merge — replaying over existing memory could duplicate history or interleave timelines, and neither has an answer the kernel could pick) and no agent should delete a store to make a command succeed. Stated rather than discovered: a bundle carries payloads as written, so a secret in memory is a secret in the committed file.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"task","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:memory-in-the-repo","observed_at":"unix:101786909200:000000000","sequence":1},{"dimension":"agentic_process","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:event-store-use-cases","observed_at":"unix:101786909200:000000000","sequence":1}],"metadata":{"writer_actor":"claude-code","writer_intent":"record_decision"}}

{"id":"project:kmp:decision:undo-is-a-write","kind":"decision","text":"Use case 3 of 3 (PR #27), and the last before 0.1.4. Undoing in KMP is a write, never a delete: a new entry saying what is true now, connected with `supersedes` (evidential) carrying why the earlier decision stopped holding. There is no delete on purpose — a memory that can be quietly edited cannot be trusted as evidence later. The write side already worked; /kmp:revert adds the part that was missing, which is showing what it buys: after the compensating write it asks (current answer leads with the new state) and rewinds to before the reversal (old decision still there with its evidence), and reports both. Refusals built in: confirm the ref before writing, because reverting the wrong entry is not undoable by a second revert; ask for the why if the user has not given one, because a supersession without a reason is a deletion with extra steps; and never improvise when someone wants an entry unfindable rather than not-current — that is a different operation, say so and stop. KEY FINDING, filed as issue #28: a superseded entry is NOT flagged in kernel_wake or kernel_ask output. contradicts IS surfaced (is_conflict() is true only for Contradicts; ask with show_conflicts returns it with full rationale), but supersession is a lifecycle fact rather than a disagreement and needs its own channel — folding it into conflicts would make every revert look like an unresolved dispute. Fix is a contract change worth batching with issue #25.","coordinates":[{"dimension":"task","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:undo-without-delete","observed_at":"unix:101786911000:000000000","sequence":1},{"dimension":"agentic_process","scope_id":"about:project:kmp:dimension:event-store-use-cases","observed_at":"unix:101786911000:000000000","sequence":1}],"metadata":{"writer_actor":"claude-code","writer_intent":"record_decision"}}

Contenido: Time Loom (dimensiones = carriles estables, entradas como marcas sobre el reloj elegido, trenza vertical cuando una entrada teje varios carriles, posición determinista por reloj+dimensión sin force layout); cuatro relojes explícitos (occurred/observed/ingested/validity) y marca HUECA cuando la entrada no lleva ese reloj, sentada en el fallback de precedencia del dominio — nunca se inventa un tiempo; escalera de zoom semántico Atlas/Episode/Moment/Evidence que cambia la representación, no el tamaño; Prisma politemporal (reality/perception/persistence/order) con hilo occurred→ingested y ausencias mostradas como ausencias; supersedes = historia atenuada frente a contradicts = bifurcación viva, nunca el mismo color de problema; navigator de panel arrastrable. Además la superficie agéntica: kmp_view_open / kmp_view_apply_intent / kmp_view_get_state (MCP pasa de 10 a 13 tools) con vocabulario CERRADO y semántico — sin x, y, camera, zoom_level ni markup, fijado por test —, view_revision propia separada de memory_revision, concurrencia optimista con expected_revision (el conflicto le dice al agente qué mira el humano para que rebase; el humano tiene preferencia), idempotencia, procedencia con explicación y undo en pantalla, refs validadas contra el store y overlays reportados como unhonored. Arquitectura: loom-core.js puro (relojes, carriles, bins, prisma, ejes) sin DOM ni renderer; view_state.rs como agregado efímero con TTL que NUNCA se escribe al store; servidor con la misma superficie /api, GET-only salvo el agregado de vista, loopback y read-only respecto a memoria; pixi 8 sigue vendorizado y hash-pinned. {"id":"project:kmp:entry:decision:embedded-kmp-has-exactly-one-storage-engine-sqlite-in-wal-mode-7ed7fecacfbcc49b","kind":"decision","text":"Embedded KMP has exactly one storage engine: SQLite in WAL mode. Released in v0.4.0 on 2026-08-28, which removed the redb dependency, its canonical-engine role, its conformance target and the legacy quality-journal importer. The `sqlite` cargo feature, the `KMP_MCP_ENGINE` selector, redb migration destinations and `share-memory` are all retired: there is no longer an engine to choose. A store written in the retired format 1 (redb) is detected by its stamped layout number and refused without being opened or modified; KMP 0.3.2 stays published as the export bridge that turns such a store into a portable `.kmp/memory.jsonl` bundle for import into a current store. {"from":"project:kmp:entry:decision:embedded-kmp-has-exactly-one-storage-engine-sqlite-in-wal-mode-7ed7fecacfbcc49b","to":"project:kmp:decision:adr-018-two-engines","rel":"supersedes","class":"evidential","why":"ADR-018 chose two engines precisely to avoid charging a C toolchain, a store migration and the static musl/Windows story to everyone 'for a problem some users have'. Use falsified that premise: sharing one embedded store between concurrently running agent hosts turned out to be the normal case rather than a minority one, so the opt-in engine became the only one anyone should run, and the seam's second implementation became permanent maintenance for a backend nobody could safely select. v0.4.0 pays exactly the cost ADR-018 rejected, once, and deletes the choice instead of maintaining it. A later reader should take ADR-018 as the correct decision for 2026-08-16 — when redb's own multi-process work was still plausibly imminent — and not as the current engine policy.","evidence":"ADR-018's own acceptance test pins the difference: two_writers_one_store.rs writes 400/400 events across two OS processes on SQLite with contiguous sequences 1..400, and asserts redb refuses the second process. The upstream redb multi-process PRs cberner/redb #1375-#1377, named in ADR-018 as the reason to wait rather than replace, had still not delivered the reader-attach half by 2026-08-28. Commit 2bfd1da removed the backend and v0.4.0 shipped it.","confidence":"high","sequence":1}
changes.reason: ADR-018 chose two engines precisely to avoid charging a C toolchain, a store migration and the static musl/Windows story to everyone 'for a problem some users have'. Use falsified that premise: sharing one embedded store between concurrently running agent hosts turned out to be the normal case rather than a minority one, so the opt-in engine became the only one anyone should run, and the seam's second implementation became permanent maintenance for a backend nobody could safely select. v0.4.0 pays exactly the cost ADR-018 rejected, once, and deletes the choice instead of maintaining it. A later reader should take ADR-018 as the correct decision for 2026-08-16 — when redb's own multi-process work was still plausibly imminent — and not as the current engine policy.
